newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MITI says watching loans to utilities.
newsitem.headline: Japan MITI says watching loans to utilities.

text.p: Trade Minister Shinji Sato said on Tuesday his ministry is watching to see if Japanese power companies receive any loans from government-affiliated financial institutions after the Japan Development Bank (JDB) is abolished.
Currently, the JDP, a government-affiliated financial institution, extends loans to power companies which use them for nuclear power plants and other energy-related projects.
JDB's loans to Japanese power firms account for nearly one-quarter of its overall loans.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday the JDP will be abolished as part of Japan's overall administrative reform.
"We are carefully watching if there will be a plan to ask other (government-affiliated) financial institutions to provide loans to power firms," Sato told a news conference.
